reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows dynamic precipitation of M23C6 and σ phase along grain boundaries in a single-phase FCC HEA during creep, but it does not address post-deposition aging of dual-phase FCC/BCC coatings, nor does it demonstrate that precipitates improve creep resistance (they are associated with a high-stress regime with higher stress exponents). The key premises about aging-induced precipitates and their beneficial effect on creep are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Nano-scale precipitates can form along grain/phase boundaries in FCC/BCC HEAs via aging
Such precipitates can pin dislocations and restrict grain boundary sliding
Dislocation pinning and grain boundary sliding restriction improve creep resistance
The cited CoCrFeNiMn HEA evidence supports precipitate-creep interaction in HEAs
